claims.claim: Identity/tradability is validated as Aurora Innovation, Inc. Class A (NASDAQ:AUR; CIK 0001828108).

Primary operating/financial lineage is Aurora's July 29, 2026 Q2 shareholder letter filed as Exhibit 99.1 to Form 8-K; current valuation is separately sourced from CompaniesMarketCap with a Sep. 18, 2026 market-cap observation.
Prior packet duplicate-origin collapse is valid: four prior evidence leaves reduce to one issuer origin; the added market source is independent of that issuer origin for valuation only.

risks.risk: Most operating evidence remains issuer-origin and therefore is not independent corroboration of issuer claims.

unknowns.unknown: Independent verification of Aurora's 2026 operating milestones remains limited in current lineage.

claims.claim: Q2 2026 revenue was $2M, operating loss $266M, operating cash use about $225M and capex $31M; Aurora ended Q2 with nearly $1.2B cash and short-term investments after issuing 30M Class A shares for $215M net proceeds through its ATM.
Aurora reaffirmed $14M-$16M 2026 revenue, with more than half expected in Q4, and targeted more than 200 driverless trucks at year-end, corresponding to about an $80M TaaS revenue run-rate.
The Q2 letter states capacity was fully allocated to the 200-truck year-end target and Aurora was negotiating with multiple customers for 2027 DaaS.
At Sep. 18, 2026 Aurora's market capitalization was about $12.64B, a demanding valuation relative to current revenue and still-unproven scaled unit economics.

risks.risk: Capital intensity and cash burn remain high while scaled gross margin and cash breakeven are unproven.
ATM issuance demonstrates real dilution dependence while commercial scale is still being established.
Back-end-loaded revenue makes manufacturing/deployment slippage material.

unknowns.unknown: Durable DaaS gross margin, customer retention economics and cash-breakeven timing are not yet demonstrated.
October manufacturing run-rate and year-end 200-truck target remain future execution checkpoints as of the cited Q2 source.

thesisQuality.basis: Commercial driverless operations, fully allocated planned capacity and customer negotiations support a strong band, but durable value capture/unit economics remain unproven.

financialOperatingMomentum.basis: Revenue is growing from a tiny base but Q2 revenue was $2M against $266M operating loss and ~$225M operating cash use; liquidity near $1.2B supports execution but dilution is active.

marketValuationOpportunity.basis: ~$12.64B market cap on Sep. 18 is demanding versus $14M-$16M 2026 revenue guidance and unproven scaled margins, placing valuation in the weak band.

catalystScore.basis: 200+ driverless-truck year-end target, planned manufacturing scale and 2027 DaaS negotiations provide multiple identifiable catalysts, though execution remains future-dated.

governancePower.basis: Management has disclosed explicit operating/cash targets and funded scaling, but repeated ATM issuance and still-unproven economics constrain a higher governance/capital-allocation assessment.

alignment2036.basis: Autonomous freight directly addresses logistics availability, safety and infrastructure efficiency; commercial driverless deployment makes this more than conceptual exposure.

crossDivisionLeverage.basis: Aurora Driver is designed as a reusable autonomy platform and current trucking deployment spans multiple customer relationships, but present economics remain concentrated in trucking scale-up.

bottleneckControl.basis: Validated driverless autonomy and integrated second-generation hardware are meaningful constrained capabilities, but manufacturing, operations, regulation and economics remain successor bottlenecks outside Aurora's sole control.

scenarioRobustness.basis: Liquidity and multiple commercial partners provide resilience, but the thesis remains materially dependent on autonomous-trucking adoption, manufacturing scale and regulatory acceptance.

substitutionResilience.basis: Driverless commercial miles and integrated hardware/software create qualification and execution barriers, but competing autonomy stacks and conventional freight remain credible substitutes.

supplyChainResilience.basis: Industrial partnerships and second-generation fleet manufacturing support scale, but current evidence does not establish broad supplier redundancy or tested contingency paths.

pricingPower.basis: Capacity allocation signals demand, but current revenue is small and scaled DaaS gross margins/contract economics are not yet demonstrated, so durable pricing power remains unproven.

riskEvidence.basis: High cash burn, ATM dilution, back-end-loaded revenue and unproven scaled unit economics create substantial execution/downside risk despite strong liquidity.

dataConfidenceEvidence.basis: Core operating and financial facts are primary-source addressed and current valuation has an independent market source; confidence is reduced because most operating claims share one issuer origin and key scaled economics remain unknown.

scoreRecord.thesis: Aurora has crossed from autonomy development into commercial driverless trucking scale-up, giving it credible exposure to a durable logistics bottleneck, but the investment case still requires successful manufacturing/deployment scale and eventual DaaS economics.
scoreRecord.keyRisk: Capital-intensive scaling, dilution and a demanding valuation can overwhelm technical progress if fleet growth, utilization or gross-margin milestones slip.
scoreRecord.nextCatalyst: Execution against the planned 1,000-truck annual manufacturing run-rate and more than 200 driverless trucks in operation by year-end 2026.

scoreBreakdown.note: earthScore records the methodology-weighted component base; risk and confidence are separately source-addressed for runtime methodology treatment.
